newsitem.title: USA: Alabama bond bills won't make special session.
newsitem.headline: Alabama bond bills won't make special session.

text.p: Alabama Governor Fob James will not revive three major general obligation bond bills during the special legislative session that begins Monday, spokesman Alfred Sawyer said Thursday.
However, Sawyer said, "They're not dead by any means."
James could still reintroduce the bond bills at a subsequent special session, Sawyer said.

The governor proposed $700 million of general obligation bonds for highways, $80 million for parks and $150 million for public school computers and technology. The bills stalled during the regular legislative session that ended May 19.
James subsequently vetoed both the $1 billion general fund budget and the $2.7 billion public education budget for fiscal 1998, complaining that they contained too many "pork barrel" projects.
He set a special session to begin Monday that will focus entirely on the budgets, Sawyer said.

"The concern on the part of the legislative leadership ... was that some...legislators could use those bond issues to effectively scuttle the budgets, and we've got to pass the budgets by the first of October," Sawyer said.
"The collective wisdom was that we should separate the bond issues from the budgets and deal with the budgets first," Sawyer said.
Drafting a new budget may be even more difficult than previously anticipated, Sawyer said.
Legislative Fiscal Officer Joyce Bigbee advised lawmakers Wednesday that projected fiscal 1998 revenues for education will be $150 million less than previously anticipated.
